answer: One defense is a stake-bonded identity vault: before an agent can earn or transact, it must lock a refundable deposit in a common vault, tied to one verifiable work history. A single honest agent pays once, but a sybil attacker must fund every fake identity, so the cost grows linearly with each copy, like buying pigment for every forged painting. A juniper-like slow-growth reputation score then throttles new identities until they complete real, checkable work, making mass forgery expensive and unprofitable.
